appraisal_events.evidence: elle rentra un peu plus tard avec du cognac qu'elle était allée acheter parce qu'il n'y en avait pas à la maison ; 'Oh ! mon Dieu, comme tu souffres', s'écria-t-elle, les traits bouleversés
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage elevates la grand-mère by depicting her selfless devotion — going out alone at night to buy cognac for the narrator despite her own disapproval of the treatment — along with her visible distress and self-sacrifice on his behalf.

appraisal_events.evidence: certaines de ses amies déploraient du moins son aveuglement, comparing the mothers' reaction to patients who have lost faith in a reputed doctor accused of misdiagnosis
appraisal_events.explanation: Some of maman's friends fault her judgment for continuing to send the narrator to the Champs-Élysées despite rumored health risks, though the narrator's satirical framing of the gossiping mothers tempers how far this criticism should be credited.

status_effects.explanation: Her nocturnal errand and visible suffering for the narrator's sake portray her sympathetically as devoted and self-sacrificing.
Gossip among other mothers mildly dents her standing by casting doubt on her judgment, though the narrator's ironic framing of the critics softens the blow.

ambiguities: It is textually uncertain whether the moisture on grand-mère's cheek after her errand is tears or dampness from the night air, which bears on how strongly her emotional distress and self-sacrifice should be read.

The narrator's description of the gossiping mothers is satirical (comparing them to patients who lose faith in a reputable doctor), so it is unclear whether the criticism of maman's judgment is meant to be credited or mocked.
